page: Amazon Web Services c5ad.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R32 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The memory configuration consists of 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, yielding a 2.0 GB per core allocation. Storage is provided via a bundled 300 GB NVMe SSD local instance store, and the instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most standard workloads. The instance achieves average ratings in Geekbench single-core (1335.0) and multi-core (5016.0) tests, as well as in Passmark CPU (10535.71) and memory (2341.68) evaluations. However, stress-ng benchmarks reveal limitations, with single-core CPU performance scoring in the bottom 10% and multi-core performance in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth also exhibits a split profile: cached small-block reads reach an average 400.52 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block reads and writes fall into the bottom 25% at 33.9 GB/sec and 21.4 GB/sec respectively.

Given its hardware profile, the c5ad.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that benefit from high-speed local NVMe storage without requiring massive memory footprints. It is appropriate for tasks such as static web serving, where it delivers an average throughput of 7.85 GB/sec, and Redis database operations, processing 7.73 million SET operations per second. It also supports light machine learning tasks, handling small 135M parameter LLM inference at average speeds, though performance drops significantly on larger 7B parameter models.
